blocks.title: Double circulation
blocks.md: Blood passes through the heart **twice** on each complete circuit of the body: the **pulmonary circulation** (heart to lungs and back) and the **systemic circulation** (heart to body and back). This keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate and allows high pressure to the body.

blocks.caption: Schematic heart (the right side of the body is on the left of the page).
blocks.alt: Four chambers: blue right atrium and right ventricle on the left, pink left atrium and left ventricle on the right, with the vena cava and pulmonary vein entering the top and the pulmonary artery and aorta leaving the bottom.

blocks.title: Path of blood
blocks.md:
Body → **vena cava** → right atrium → (tricuspid valve) → right ventricle → **pulmonary artery** → lungs → **pulmonary vein** → left atrium → (bicuspid valve) → left ventricle → **aorta** → body.

The **left ventricle** has the thickest wall because it pumps blood to the whole body. **Valves** stop backflow. The heart muscle is supplied by the **coronary arteries**.

blocks.title: Blood vessels
blocks.md:
- **Arteries**: carry blood away from the heart; thick, muscular, elastic walls; narrow lumen; blood at high pressure; pulse felt.
- **Veins**: carry blood to the heart; thin walls; wide lumen; **valves**; low pressure.
- **Capillaries**: walls one cell thick, very narrow; exchange of materials between blood and cells.

Pulmonary vessels are the exception: the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood, the pulmonary vein oxygenated blood.

blocks.title: Heart health (flag for health review)
blocks.md: Risk factors for coronary heart disease include smoking, a diet rich in saturated fat and salt, lack of exercise and stress. Regular exercise, a balanced diet and not smoking lower the risk. Anyone with chest pain should seek medical help.

blocks.title: Cardiac output
blocks.statement: A resting heart pumps 70 cm³ of blood per beat and beats 72 times per minute. Calculate the volume pumped per minute (cardiac output).
steps: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate.

blocks.title: Following a blood cell
blocks.statement: Trace a red blood cell from the left ventricle to a muscle in the leg and back to the heart.
steps: Left ventricle → aorta → arteries → capillaries in the leg muscle (oxygen is released).
Deoxygenated blood → veins → vena cava → right atrium.
blocks.answer: Left ventricle → aorta → artery → muscle capillary → vein → vena cava → right atrium.

blocks.title: Components of blood
blocks.md: Blood is a tissue made of **plasma** (about 55 % of the volume) and **blood cells**. Plasma is a pale yellow liquid, mostly water, that carries dissolved glucose, amino acids, mineral ions, hormones, urea, plasma proteins and carbon dioxide (as hydrogencarbonate ions), and distributes heat.

blocks.caption: The cells of the blood.
blocks.alt: Four drawings: a red blood cell with a pale centre and no nucleus, a phagocyte with a lobed nucleus, a lymphocyte with a large round nucleus and some small platelets.

blocks.title: Cells and their jobs
blocks.md:
- **Red blood cells**: biconcave discs without a nucleus, full of **haemoglobin**. In the lungs haemoglobin combines with oxygen to form **oxyhaemoglobin**; in the tissues it releases it.
- **White blood cells**: **phagocytes** engulf and digest microbes (phagocytosis); **lymphocytes** make **antibodies**.
- **Platelets**: fragments of cells that help the blood **clot**, sealing a wound.

blocks.title: Defence
blocks.md: Antibodies are made by lymphocytes in response to **antigens** (molecules on microbes). Each antibody fits one antigen, sticks microbes together or marks them for destruction. After an infection, some lymphocytes remain as **memory cells** that respond fast if the same microbe returns: this is the basis of **immunity**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Red blood cells have *no nucleus*; white cells do.
- Haemoglobin is in the red cells, not in the plasma.
- Platelets are cell fragments, not full cells.
- Blood is not always 'blue' inside the body: deoxygenated blood is dark red.

blocks.title: Percentage plasma
blocks.statement: A 10 cm³ sample of blood is spun in a centrifuge and 5.5 cm³ of clear yellow liquid separates from the cells. Calculate the percentage of plasma.

blocks.title: A cut on the knee
blocks.statement: A boy falls in Buea and cuts his knee. Describe how the blood protects him.
steps: Platelets help form a clot of fibres that seals the wound and stops bleeding.
Phagocytes engulf microbes that enter; lymphocytes make specific antibodies against them.
blocks.answer: Clotting stops blood loss and microbes entering; white cells destroy microbes that get in.
